journalPosts.author: Camille Laurent
journalPosts.title: The Art of Hanging Floor-to-Ceiling Linen Drapery
journalPosts.excerpt: How ceiling-mounted tracks, double fullness, and translucent Belgian flax soften architectural proportions and sculpt shifting daylight.
journalPosts.body:
Architectural drapery does more than frame a window—it alters the acoustics, vertical scale, and emotional temperature of an entire room. When linen panels rise unbroken from ceiling shadow-gap to floor, a modest apartment gains the serene cadence of a sunlit European salon.

At LOOMÉ, we recommend mounting discreet recessed tracks flush with the ceiling line and specifying at least 2.2x fabric fullness so unbleached Belgian flax falls in calm, uninterrupted vertical columns. Avoid skimping on width: generous fullness creates soft rhythmic shadows even when curtains are drawn open beside the glass.

For the hem, allow a tailored 1.5 cm kiss at the floor in minimalist spaces with stone or oak boards, or request a relaxed 5 cm break when pairing heavy double-lined drapery with antique plaster walls. Finish with weighted blind-stitched hems so every breeze moves the weave gracefully without losing poise.

journalPosts.author: Elena Marchetti
journalPosts.title: The Quiet Ritual of Caring for European Flax Linen
journalPosts.excerpt: Gentle laundering temperatures, pH-neutral soaps, and shaded line-drying habits that make stonewashed bedding more luminous with every year.
journalPosts.body:
Unlike mass-produced textiles coated in synthetic softeners that wash away after three cycles, genuine long-staple Normandy flax improves organically with age. Its hollow fiber structure releases moisture swiftly and naturally resists pilling when treated with unhurried care.

Wash stonewashed duvet sets and sheets at 30°C on a gentle cycle with a mild, optical-brightener-free liquid detergent. Give linen ample space inside the drum so water circulates freely through the weave, and skip fabric softeners altogether—they coat flax fibers and diminish breathability.

Remove linens promptly while barely damp, shake them once to release deep creases, and line-dry in dappled shade away from harsh midday glare. If you prefer a crisper editorial finish on drapery or table runners, steam vertically from the reverse side rather than pressing with a dry high-heat iron.

journalPosts.author: Henrik Lindholm
journalPosts.title: Inside the Heritage Loom: Four Generations of Belgian Weaving
journalPosts.excerpt: A study of slow shuttle tension, yarn-dyed selvedge edges, and the tactile precision behind 60,000-rub heirloom upholstery.
journalPosts.body:
Step inside a fourth-generation weaving mill in West Flanders and the first sensation is rhythmic quietness. Rather than racing modern air-jet machines to maximum output, heritage looms run at deliberate speeds that preserve the subtle organic slub of long-staple European flax.

Every warp thread is tensioned by hand and inspected under north-facing daylight before a single yard enters production. For upholstery weaves like our Como herringbone, virgin wool and heavy flax yarns are twisted tightly prior to weaving, achieving over 60,000 Martindale rubs without sacrificing a soft, welcoming hand.

Once off the loom, each bolt rests before finishing: hand-mitred drapery corners, mother-of-pearl duvet closures, and raw selvedge fringes are completed by atelier seamstresses who sign off every piece individually.

journalPosts.author: Claire Beaumont
journalPosts.title: From Normandy Dew-Retting to Zero-Waste Atelier Bolts
journalPosts.excerpt: Why rain-fed flax cultivation, biodegradable natural fibers, and small-batch mill runs define enduring sustainable luxury.
journalPosts.body:
True sustainability in interiors begins long before a textile reaches a showroom—it starts in coastal northern European fields where flax thrives on natural rainfall alone, requiring zero artificial irrigation and virtually no chemical inputs.

After harvest, stalks lie across the earth for slow dew-retting: morning mist and gentle sunlight naturally loosen the woody core from the silky bast fibers inside. Every part of the plant is utilized, from long fibers spun into drapery yarn to shorter tow fibers transformed into heavyweight upholstery and paper.

At LOOMÉ, our mills weave in disciplined small batches certified to OEKO-TEX Standard 100. Off-cuts from custom drapery commissions are never discarded—they become our client swatch boxes and limited-edition lumbar cushions, honoring every meter of fiber grown.

journalPosts.author: LOOMÉ Editorial Studio
journalPosts.title: Layering Ivory, Sage Olive & Champagne in Calm Rooms
journalPosts.excerpt: A tactile guide to balancing matte bouclé, washed velvet, and sheer linen so quiet monochrome spaces glow from dawn to dusk.
journalPosts.body:
Monochrome interiors sing when contrast comes from weave architecture rather than loud pattern. Pair a crisp 165 GSM sheer Belgian linen against heavy wool-linen herringbone upholstery, then anchor the seating group with a single muted sage olive velvet lumbar cushion and a hand-loomed champagne merino throw.

Because each fiber absorbs and reflects daylight differently—matte stonewashed flax softening glare while cotton sateen and washed velvet catch gentle highlights—the room shifts subtly across the day without ever feeling busy.

Always test swatches vertically as well as flat on a table: a warm ivory drapery that reads creamy beside oak flooring will take on luminous alabaster notes once backlit by afternoon sun.

textileCarePage.heading: The Art of Textile Care
textileCarePage.intro: Natural fibers reward unhurried stewardship. Explore our atelier guidance for laundering, drying, steaming, storing, and preserving European flax linen, organic cotton, washed velvet, mulberry silk, and tailored upholstery.
textileCarePage.labelReminderHeading: Always Follow Your Product Care Label
textileCarePage.labelReminderBody: This guide offers accurate general care advice for pure natural textiles. Because custom drapery linings, yarn-dyed trims, and specialty blends may require tailored handling, always follow the individual care label sewn into your specific LOOMÉ piece.

fabrics.name: Linen
fabrics.subtitle: Stonewashed European flax bedding, table linens & architectural drapery
fabrics.quickSummary: 30°C Gentle Wash · Shade Line Dry · Steam Damp
fabrics.washing: Machine wash separately or with similar neutrals at 30°C (85°F) on a gentle cycle using a mild, pH-neutral liquid detergent free of optical brighteners or bleach. Leave generous space in the drum so flax fibers rinse cleanly.
fabrics.drying: Remove promptly while slightly damp and give each piece a gentle shake to relax creases. Line dry in dappled shade or lay flat; if tumble drying bedding, use the lowest heat setting and remove before completely dry.
fabrics.ironing: Embrace linen's relaxed drape naturally, or steam vertically while barely damp. For a crisp table or curtain finish, iron on medium-high heat from the reverse side using steam.
fabrics.storage: Store completely dry in a cool, ventilated linen closet wrapped in breathable unbleached cotton bags rather than sealed plastic, which can trap humidity and yellow natural flax.
fabrics.maintenance: Avoid fabric softeners—they coat flax fibers and reduce breathability. Rotate bedding sets weekly and shake drapery periodically to release settled household dust.
fabrics.atelierNote: Genuine European flax grows noticeably softer and more luminous with every gentle wash, developing an heirloom drape over years of daily use.

fabrics.name: Cotton
fabrics.subtitle: 600-thread-count organic cotton sateen sheets, pillowcases & woven throws
fabrics.quickSummary: 30–40°C Delicate Wash · Low Tumble · Warm Press
fabrics.washing: Wash organic cotton sateen in cool to warm water (30–40°C) on a delicate cycle with mild plant-based detergent. Turn duvet covers and pillowcases inside out and fasten buttons before laundering to protect the lustrous satin weave.
fabrics.drying: Line dry outdoors away from direct harsh midday sun to preserve ivory and champagne tones, or tumble dry on low heat and remove immediately while softly warm to minimize creasing.
fabrics.ironing: Press on a medium cotton setting with light steam while slightly damp, gliding along the weave direction to restore sateen's fluid sheen. Avoid high dry heat on satin-stitched borders.
fabrics.storage: Fold neatly once thoroughly cooled and dry, placing heavier sheets at the base of the stack. Tuck a natural cedar block or dried lavender sachet nearby for lasting freshness.
fabrics.maintenance: Wash separately from rough terry towels or garments with zippers to prevent surface abrasion and pilling. Blot spills immediately with cool water before laundering.
fabrics.atelierNote: Shaking organic sateen sheets smooth immediately after the spin cycle dramatically reduces creases and preserves their cool, whisper-soft hand.

fabrics.name: Velvet
fabrics.subtitle: Matte Italian cotton-viscose washed velvet cushions & accent panels
fabrics.quickSummary: Specialist Dry Clean · Never Iron Pile · Gentle Steam
fabrics.washing: Professional specialist dry cleaning is strongly recommended for velvet covers and drapery to protect pile luster and prevent water spotting. Remove feather inserts via the concealed zip before cleaning.
fabrics.drying: Never wring, twist, or tumble dry velvet. If lightly spot-blotted, allow the fabric to air dry naturally away from radiators or direct sunlight, then restore the pile once fully dry.
fabrics.ironing: Never press an iron directly onto the velvet face—direct heat and weight permanently crush the nap. Instead, hold a handheld steamer a few centimeters away on the reverse side and lightly brush the pile upward.
fabrics.storage: Hang velvet drapery on padded hangers or fold loosely with acid-free tissue paper between layers so the pile never rests under heavy weight, which can leave lasting pressure marks.
fabrics.maintenance: Vacuum lightly every few weeks using a soft upholstery brush nozzle moving in the direction of the nap. Fluff cushion inserts regularly and rotate exposure to bright window light.
fabrics.atelierNote: If shipping or storage leaves a light crease in velvet, hanging the cover in a gently steamy bathroom often relaxes the pile effortlessly without touching the surface.

fabrics.name: Silk
fabrics.subtitle: Luminous mulberry silk accents, sheer interior veils & delicate trims
fabrics.quickSummary: Dry Clean or Cool Hand Wash · Flat Shade Dry · Low Reverse Steam
fabrics.washing: Consult the piece's care label first: structured or lined silk pieces should be professionally dry cleaned. Unlined washable silk may be hand-washed gently in cool water (under 30°C) using a pH-neutral silk detergent—never soak longer than five minutes.
fabrics.drying: Never wring silk fibers. Press excess water gently between two clean white cotton towels, then lay flat on a dry surface in cool shade away from direct sunlight and heating vents.
fabrics.ironing: Steam lightly from the reverse side using distilled water at a low distance, or press on the lowest silk setting on the reverse side with a clean cotton pressing cloth and no water droplets that could leave rings.
fabrics.storage: Store silk in breathable cotton garment bags or wrapped in acid-free tissue paper in a dark, dry drawer. Avoid wire hangers, cedar oil contact, and direct perfumes or room sprays.
fabrics.maintenance: Air silk textiles gently after use rather than over-cleaning. Shield sheer silk drapery from prolonged direct UV light with solar shades or lined backing to preserve fiber tensile strength.
fabrics.atelierNote: Because silk is a natural protein fiber, enzyme-based detergents and alkaline soaps weaken its sheen—always choose a dedicated silk wash or trusted specialty cleaner.

fabrics.name: Upholstery
fabrics.subtitle: Heavyweight Italian herringbone, wool-flax blends & sculptural bouclé
fabrics.quickSummary: Weekly Soft Vacuum · Blot Spills Immediately · Annual Pro Clean
fabrics.washing: Fixed upholstery and heavyweight wool-linen bolts should never be machine washed. For routine refreshing or deep cleaning, engage a certified upholstery specialist familiar with natural flax and wool blends.
fabrics.drying: After blotting a fresh spill, allow the area to dry evenly in ambient room airflow. Never apply hairdryers or concentrated heat, which can shrink natural yarns or set organic stains.
fabrics.ironing: Tailored upholstery requires no routine ironing. Removable heavy linen slipcovers—only where permitted by the product care label—may be gently steamed in place while slightly damp for a crisp tailored silhouette.
fabrics.storage: Store spare yardage bolts rolled right-side-in on cardboard tubes wrapped in breathable cotton sheeting, kept flat off the floor in a climate-stable, moth-protected room.
fabrics.maintenance: Vacuum weekly with a low-suction soft brush attachment to lift fine dust before it abrades yarns. Rotate seat and back cushions monthly for even wear, and blot spills gently with a clean white damp cloth—never rub.
fabrics.atelierNote: Consistent light vacuuming is the single most effective habit for upholstery longevity, preventing microscopic grit from wearing down heavyweight bouclé and herringbone weaves.

textileCarePage.tipsIntro: Small, deliberate habits protect fiber integrity, subtle neutral tones, and tailored architectural drape across decades of daily living.

careTips.question: How should I treat spills on natural linen, cotton, or upholstery?
careTips.answer: Act promptly by blotting—never rubbing—with an undyed absorbent cloth or paper towel to lift excess liquid. Work from the outer edge of the spill inward with cool water so the mark does not spread. Avoid chlorine bleach and harsh optical brighteners, which weaken natural cellulose and protein fibers and leave pale halos on warm ivory or sage weaves. For red wine, oil, or delicate velvet and silk, consult a trusted textile specialist promptly.

careTips.question: Why does LOOMÉ advise against synthetic fabric softeners?
careTips.answer: Commercial fabric softeners coat natural fibers in silicone and waxy compounds that create artificial slipperiness while clogging the breathable hollow core of European flax and organic cotton. Over time, this buildup traps detergent residue, dulls natural luster, and reduces moisture absorption. Cool gentle washing, ample drum room, and natural wool dryer balls keep textiles effortlessly soft without residue.

careTips.question: Should I steam or iron floor-to-ceiling linen curtains?
careTips.answer: For installed drapery, vertical steaming from the reverse side using distilled water is the gentlest and most effective way to release transit creases while maintaining soft architectural folds. Hang panels for 48 hours first so natural gravity relaxes the weave, then glide the steamer downward without tugging the hem. Reserve flat ironing for table linens or tailored borders where the care label permits medium heat.

careTips.question: How can I protect curtains and upholstery from direct sunlight?
careTips.answer: All natural fibers—especially silk, washed velvet, and yarn-dyed linen—respond gradually to intense ultraviolet light. Pair sheer drapery with discreet UV-filtering window film or layered lined panels in south- and west-facing rooms, and rotate cushions, throws, and sofa seats every few weeks so daylight softens surfaces evenly over time.

careTips.question: What is the best way to store seasonal bedding and throws?
careTips.answer: Always launder or air textiles completely before seasonal storage—even invisible oils or humidity can cause discoloration over months. Ensure every piece is thoroughly dry, fold loosely to avoid permanent crease stress, and place inside breathable unbleached cotton storage bags with natural cedar or lavender. Avoid sealed plastic bins or damp basements.

textileCarePage.longevityHeading: Woven to Soften, Made to Endure
textileCarePage.longevityBody:
Fine textiles are not meant to be kept untouched behind glass—they are crafted to live beside you, softening with every season and gathering quiet character as light moves across a room.

When long-staple Normandy flax, GOTS-certified organic cotton, and heritage-loomed wool blends are cared for gently—washed cool, dried in shade, and stored in breathable air—their fibers relax without losing structural poise. Caring well for natural textiles is both a daily sensory ritual and the most meaningful expression of sustainable living.

shippingFaqs.question: How will I receive tracking details once my order ships?
shippingFaqs.answer: As soon as your parcel leaves our atelier and is scanned by our courier partner, our concierge shares your tracking reference via WhatsApp or email so you can follow delivery progress to your door.

shippingFaqs.question: Do custom drapery panels or cut-to-order fabrics take longer to ship?
shippingFaqs.answer: Yes. Ready-to-ship bedding and cushions are prepared first, whereas made-to-measure drapery, weighted hems, and continuous yardage bolts require dedicated atelier finishing. Your estimated completion date is confirmed before production begins.

shippingFaqs.question: Can I update my delivery address after placing an order?
shippingFaqs.answer: If your parcel has not yet been handed to the courier, message our concierge promptly with your name and order details and we will gladly update your delivery instructions.

shippingFaqs.question: How are fine linen and velvet pieces protected in transit?
shippingFaqs.answer: Textiles are folded cleanly in acid-free paper and breathable cotton wraps inside reinforced outer cartons so natural fibers arrive fresh, dry, and ready to hang or steam.

shippingFaqs.question: Do you deliver to regional, international, or interior-trade job sites?
shippingFaqs.answer: Delivery coverage, trade receiving-warehouse coordination, and international courier options are arranged according to your location. Reach out via WhatsApp with your postal code for a tailored delivery quote.

returnPillars.title: Eligible Textiles
returnPillars.description: Ready-to-ship bedding, cushions, throws, and standard-size curtains in unused condition are eligible for return or exchange according to store policy. Made-to-measure drapery and custom-cut fabric yardage are generally final sale unless faulty.

returnPillars.title: Return Request Timeframe
returnPillars.description: Please contact our concierge within our merchant-configured return window following delivery. Share your order details and preferred outcome—exchange, store credit, or refund—so we can provide return instructions.

returnPillars.title: Original Condition & Packaging
returnPillars.description: Items must be returned unwashed, unused, unaltered, and free from fragrance or wear, folded neatly inside their original protective bags with all care labels and tags intact.

returnPillars.title: Inspection & Reimbursement
returnPillars.description: Once your parcel arrives back at our atelier, our team inspects the textiles promptly. Approved exchanges are dispatched swiftly, and approved refunds are processed back via your agreed payment method within our standard review timeframe.

shippingReturnsPage.damagedIntro: Every piece is inspected by hand before leaving LOOMÉ. In the rare event that your parcel arrives damaged in transit or contains an incorrect size, color, or item, we will prioritize making it right.

damagedSteps.title: Inspect Parcel Upon Arrival

damagedSteps.title: Share Photos & Order Reference
damagedSteps.description: Send clear photographs of the item, care label, and packaging along with your order details to our concierge via WhatsApp or email.

damagedSteps.title: Priority Replacement or Resolution

faqPage.intro: Thoughtful guidance on ordering LOOMÉ textiles, delivery coordination, return and exchange care, natural fiber upkeep, and made-to-measure drapery commissions.

items.question: How does ordering through the LOOMÉ Private Checkout work?
items.answer: Add your chosen textiles, colors, and dimensions to your Shopping Bag and proceed to Checkout. Submitting your delivery details prepares a formatted order summary directly for our concierge via WhatsApp, where our team confirms stock availability, delivery charges, and payment arrangements personally.

items.question: Can I modify sizes, colors, or quantities after submitting an order request?
items.answer: Yes—because every order is reviewed personally by our concierge before dispatch or cutting, simply message us as soon as possible with your updated preferences and we will adjust your selection prior to confirmation.

items.question: How are delivery timelines and shipping charges determined?
items.answer: Shipping charges and estimated transit windows vary by destination, parcel weight, and whether items are ready-to-ship or made-to-measure. Your exact courier option, shipping quote, and estimated dispatch schedule are confirmed directly with your order.

items.question: Will I receive tracking details once my textiles are dispatched?
items.answer: Yes. Once your pieces are folded in breathable protective wrapping and handed to our courier partner, our concierge shares your tracking information via WhatsApp or email so you can follow delivery progress.

items.question: Which textiles are eligible for return or exchange?
items.answer: Unused, unwashed ready-to-live textiles in their original condition and packaging are eligible within our store's configured return window. Bespoke drapery panels, custom-hemmed curtains, and cut-to-order yardage are generally final sale unless an item arrives faulty or incorrect.

items.question: How do I request a return, exchange, or assistance with a damaged parcel?
items.answer: Reach out to our concierge via WhatsApp or the Contact page with your order reference and, for damaged or incorrect deliveries, clear photographs of the item and packaging. Our team will walk you through return authorization, inspection, and resolution promptly.

items.question: How should I launder European flax linen and organic cotton bedding?
items.answer: In general, wash pure flax linen and organic cotton sateen cool on a gentle cycle using a mild, pH-neutral detergent without bleach or synthetic fabric softeners, then line dry in dappled shade. Always consult the specific care label sewn into your piece for tailored instructions.

items.question: How should velvet cushions, silk veils, and heavyweight upholstery be maintained?
items.answer: For dense velvet, structured silk, and tailored upholstery weaves, specialist professional cleaning is typically recommended. Avoid pressing an iron directly onto velvet pile—use gentle reverse steaming and light soft-brush vacuuming in the direction of the nap, following your item's sewn-in care label.

items.question: Do you offer made-to-measure drapery panels and custom fabric yardage?
items.answer: Yes. Our atelier tailors floor-to-ceiling curtains with custom drop lengths, lining weights, and pinch-pleat or wave-fold headings, as well as continuous yardage bolts for interior architects and residential projects. Share your window measurements via WhatsApp or our Contact page to begin.

items.question: Can I request fabric swatches before placing a bespoke or upholstery order?
items.answer: Certainly. Natural weaves respond subtly to morning and evening daylight, so we encourage viewing physical cuttings against your walls and flooring first. Contact our concierge to request curated textile swatches for your project.

about.heading: Woven with Quiet Reverence for Material & Light
about.body: Founded as an editorial textile maison, LOOMÉ partners with family-owned weaving mills across Belgium, Northern Italy, and Portugal. We create architectural drapery, tactile bedding, and heirloom fabrics designed to bring calm, warmth, and enduring beauty to everyday living.
about.collageDescription: From raw Normandy flax stalks to final steam-pressed drapery panels, every stage honors slow craft.
about.history: We reject disposable decor in favor of honest natural fibers that deepen in character with time. Each palette is formulated to harmonize effortlessly with travertine, oak, plaster, and shifting natural daylight.

servicesPage.heading: Bespoke Collections & Atelier Services
servicesPage.intro: Beyond our ready-to-live editions, our textile specialists offer tailored drapery, upholstery sourcing, and trade consultations.

services.name: Bespoke Architectural Drapery
services.description: Made-to-measure pinch-pleat and wave-fold curtains tailored precisely to ceiling height, light filtration needs, and window geometry.

services.name: Curated Swatch Atelier
services.description: Experience the weight, slub, and daylight response of our finest weaves in your own space before committing to yardage.

services.name: Trade & Interior Architect Program
services.description: Dedicated yardage allocations, custom dye lots, and concierge logistics for residential and boutique hospitality projects.
